questions.question: Who founded the value of ‘G’?
questions.questionHtml: Who founded the value of ‘G’?
questions.solution: The value of 'G' is the gravitational constant, which is involved in the calculation of gravitational effects in Sir Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation and Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity. The measured value of the constant is known with certainty to four significant digits and its value in SI units is approximately 6.674×10−11 m3⋅kg−1⋅s−2. The modern notation of Newton's law involving 'G' was introduced by C.V. Boys, and the first implicit measurement with an accuracy within about 1% is attributed to Henry Cavendish in a 1798 experiment. Therefore, the correct answer is 'Henry Cavendish'.

questions.question: Who introduced the concept of virtual water?
questions.questionHtml: Who introduced the concept of virtual water?
questions.solution: John Anthony Allan introduced the concept of virtual water, which refers to the hidden flow of water when food or commodities are traded. This concept is crucial for understanding the amount of water used in production and trade, especially important for water-scarce regions and global water management strategies. Allan was awarded the Stockholm Water Prize in 2008 for his contribution.

questions.question: Who started the chemical revolution in the 18 th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature?
questions.questionHtml: Who started the chemical revolution in the 18<sup>th</sup> century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier

Key Points

  • Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier is widely regarded as the father of modern chemistry.
  • He was instrumental in the chemical revolution of the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature.
  • Lavoisier's work laid the foundation for the law of conservation of mass, which states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
  • He also helped develop the modern system for naming chemical substances, which replaced the older, less systematic names.
  • His contributions significantly advanced the field of chemistry and helped transition it from alchemy to a more empirical and systematic science.

Additional Information

  • Joseph Priestley also discovered oxygen independently around the same time as Lavoisier, but did not recognize it as an element.
  • Dame Kathleen Lonsdale was a renowned crystallographer, not directly related to the chemical revolution.
  • Svante August Arrhenius was a Swedish scientist known for his theory of electrolytic dissociation and contributions to physical chemistry, but he was active in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

questions.solution: Heinrich Hertz, a German physicist, confirmed James Clerk Maxwell's theories by producing and receiving radio waves in 1886. Maxwell had previously predicted the existence of these waves in the 1870s. Hertz's work laid the foundation for Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi, who built the first commercially successful wireless telegraphy system in 1895.

questions.question: Who described in 1662 that when a gas was pumped into an enclosed space, it would shrink to fit in that space, but the pressure exerted by the gas on the container would increase?
questions.questionHtml: Who described in 1662 that when a gas was pumped into an enclosed space, it would shrink to fit in that space, but the pressure exerted by the gas on the container would increase?
questions.solution: Robert Boyle (1627—91) studied the behavior of gases enclosed in a chamber and formulated the gas law named after him. questions.question: When did Ernest Rutherford publish the results of the gold-foil experiment, which showed that scattering is caused by a rigid, dense core at the centre of the atom - the nucleus?

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic radiation was discovered by Johann Wilhelm Ritter in 1801?
questions.questionHtml: Which type of electromagnetic radiation was discovered by Johann Wilhelm Ritter in 1801?
questions.solution: Johann Wilhelm Ritter discovered ultraviolet (UV) radiation in 1801 while experimenting with silver chloride, which darkened when exposed to light beyond the violet spectrum. This was the first identification of electromagnetic radiation beyond the visible spectrum. UV radiation is categorized into three types based on wavelength: UVA (320-400 nm), which penetrates the skin deeply and causes aging; UVB (290-320 nm), responsible for sunburn and skin cancer; and UVC (100-290 nm), the most harmful but mostly absorbed by the ozone layer. In contrast, X-rays are used in medical imaging, infrared in heating and night vision, and gamma rays in cancer treatment.

questions.question: Who among the following made the first the compound microscope?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following made the first the compound microscope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Zacharias Janssen.

Key Points

  • A Dutch father-son team named Hans and Zacharias Janssen invented the first so-called compound microscope in the late 16th century when they discovered that if they put a lens at the top and bottom of a tube and looked through it, objects on the other end became magnified.
  • A compound microscope is a high-power (high magnification) microscope that uses a compound lens system.
  • A compound microscope has multiple lenses: the objective lens is compounded (multiplied) by the eyepiece lens to obtain a high magnification.
  • Higher magnification is achieved by using two lenses rather than just a single magnifying lens.

Additional Information

  • Components of the compound microscope:
    • Eyepiece: ​Also known as the ocular, is the lens that you look through at the top of the microscope. Standard eyepieces typically have a 10x magnification power.
    • Eyepiece Tube: The eyepieces are held in place above the objective lens by the Eyepiece Tube. A diopter adjustment ring is frequently included in binocular microscope heads to account for probable irregularities in human eyesight in one or both eyes. A diopter is not required when using a monocular (single eye) microscope.
    • Objective Lenses: These are the primary optical lenses on a microscope. 
    • Nosepiece: It houses the objectives. The objectives are exposed and are mounted on a rotating turret so that different objectives can be conveniently selected.
    • Coarse and Fine Focus knobs: These are used to focus the microscope.
    • Stage: The specimen to be examined is put on the stage. When working at greater magnifications, when careful motions of the specimen slide are necessary, a mechanical stage is used.
    • Stage clips: When there is no mechanical stage, stage clips are employed. To observe different areas of the specimen, the viewer must manually move the slide.
    • Aperture: The opening in the stage through which the base (transmitted) light reaches the stage is known as an aperture.
    • Illuminator: It is a light source for a microscope that is normally situated in the microscope's base. Low-voltage halogen bulbs with continuous variable illumination control are used in most light microscopes.
    • Condenser: The light from the illuminator is collected and focused on the specimen by the condenser. It's usually found beneath the stage, along with an iris diaphragm.
    • Iris Diaphragm: The amount of light that reaches the specimen is controlled by the Iris Diaphragm. It's beneath the stage and above the condenser. An Abbe condenser with an iris diaphragm is standard on most high-end microscopes.
    • Condenser Focus Knob: It adjusts the lighting focus on the specimen by moving the condenser up or down.

questions.question: Researchers of Kerala-based Amrita University in collaboration with the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority have developed a real-time _______. This system can help save lives and prevent loss to property by issuing advance alerts.
questions.questionHtml: Researchers of Kerala-based Amrita University in collaboration with the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority have developed a real-time _______. This system can help save lives and prevent loss to property by issuing advance alerts.
questions.solution:
• Researchers of Kerala-based Amrita University in collaboration with the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority have developed a real-time Landslide warning system.
  • The system gives advance warnings of landslides so that people can be safely evacuated before disaster strikes.
  • After successfully deploying India’s first such system in Kerala’s Western Ghats, it will now be deployed in Sikkim to guard against rainfall-induced landslides in the Sikkim-Darjeeling belt. 
  • The system collects real-time, continuous data from the sensors, performs basic analysis at the Field Management Center (FMC) located on the site in Sikkim and relays it to the Data Management Center (DMC) at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham in Kerala’s Kollam district.
  • The project is jointly funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India, and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham.
  • Extra:-
  • In 2008, Amrita set up India's first landslide laboratory which can create small landslides under controlled conditions and act as the feedback system for field deployment.
  • Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham has been ranked 8th among the Indian universities by NIRF in 2019.

questions.question: On 12 September 2002, ISRO launched the Kalpana-1 satellite using the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle. What is the application of this satellite?
questions.questionHtml: On 12 September 2002, ISRO launched the Kalpana-1 satellite using the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle. What is the application of this satellite?
questions.solution: The Kalpana-1 satellite, launched by ISRO on 12 September 2002 using the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, is primarily used for climate and environment communication. Named after Kalpana Chawla, it aids in meteorological observations and data collection related to weather and climate. It plays a crucial role in disaster management by providing data for forecasting and monitoring natural calamities like cyclones and floods. Originally known as METSAT-1, it operates in geostationary orbit, supporting agriculture, water resources management, and aviation through its instruments, including a Very High Resolution Radiometer (VHRR) and a Data Relay Transponder (DRT).

questions.question: Who was famous for the invention of the vacuum pump in the 17 th century and also pioneered the concept of the absolute vacuum of space, measured the weight of air and used air pressure to predict the weather?
questions.questionHtml: Who was famous for the invention of the vacuum pump in the 17<sup>th </sup>century and also pioneered the concept of the absolute vacuum of space, measured the weight of air and used air pressure to predict the weather?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Otto von Guericke.

Key Points

  • Otto von Guericke was famous for the invention of the vacuum pump in the 17th century and also pioneered the concept of the absolute vacuum of space, measuring the weight of air and using air pressure to predict the weather.
  • In 1650 von Guericke invented the vacuum pump. His model consisted of a piston and an air gun cylinder with two-way flaps designed to pull air out of whatever vessel it was connected to, and used to investigate the properties of the vacuum in many experiments.
  • A particular and repeated target of his criticism is the manner in which the "nature abhors a vacuum" principle had migrated from simply a matter of experiment to a high principle of physics which could be invoked to explain phenomena such as suction but which itself was above question.
  • Von Guericke was a very pious man in the Dionysian tradition and attributed the vacuum of space to the creations and designs of an infinite divinity. 
  • Otto von Guericke showed that substances were not pulled by a vacuum, but were pushed by the pressure of the surrounding fluids.

Additional Information

  • Sir John Douglas Cockcroft was a British physicist who shared with Ernest Walton the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1951 for splitting the atomic nucleus and was instrumental in the development of nuclear power.
  • Enrico Fermi was an Italian physicist and the creator of the world's first nuclear reactor, the Chicago Pile-1. He has been called the "architect of the nuclear age" and the "architect of the atomic bomb".
  • Valerianus Magnus was an Italian Capuchin, missionary preacher in Central Europe, polemicist and author.

questions.question: Which German chemist was the first to show a graphical representation of the periodicity of an atomic volume plotted against atomic weight?
questions.questionHtml: Which German chemist was the first to show a graphical representation of the periodicity of an atomic volume plotted against atomic weight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lothar Meyer

Key Points

  • Julius Lothar Meyer:-
    • He was a German chemist who was one of the pioneers in developing the earliest versions of the periodic table of the chemical elements.
    • He worked independently of, but simultaneously with, Dmitri Mendeleev, and both published their versions of the periodic table in 1869.
    • He first showed a graphical representation of the periodicity of an atomic volume plotted against atomic weight.  
    • He published his findings in 1864, a few years before Dmitri Mendeleev published his more famous periodic table. 

Additional Information

  • John Newlands:-
    • He was an English chemist who developed a system for classifying the elements that is known as the "Law of Octaves".
    • Newlands' system was based on the observation that every eighth element had similar properties to the first element.
    • This observation was later confirmed by Dmitri Mendeleev's periodic table, and Newlands is now considered one of the pioneers of the periodic law.
  • William Ramsay:-
    • He was a Scottish chemist who is best known for his discovery of the noble gases.
    • Ramsay discovered helium, neon, argon, krypton, and xenon, and he shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Lord Rayleigh in 1904 for his work on the noble gases.
  • Glenn Theodore Seaborg:-
    • He was an American nuclear chemist who synthesized transuranium elements.
    • Seaborg synthesized 10 transuranium elements, including plutonium, americium, berkelium, californium, einsteinium, fermium, mendelevium, nobelium, lawrencium, and rutherfordium.
    • He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 for his work on the transuranium elements.

questions.question: In the Millikan’s Oil Drop experiment, the oil drop is subjected to such forces whose nature does NOT fall under the category of:
questions.questionHtml: In the Millikan’s Oil Drop experiment, the oil drop is subjected to such forces whose nature does NOT fall under the category of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is magnetostatic.

Key Points

  •  In 1913, the American physicist R. A. Millikan performed the pioneering oil-drop experiment for the precise measurement of the charge on an electron. He found that the charge on an oil-droplet was always an integral multiple of an elementary charge, 1.602 × 10-19 C. Millikan’s experiment established that electric charge is quantized. From the values of charge (e) and specific charge(e/m ), the mass (m) of the electron could be determined.
  • In the experiment a tiny charged droplets of oil was suspended between two metal electrodes. The pull of downward gravitational force was balanced with the help of upward drag and electric forces. The density of the oil, electric field and mass was known, with the help of these known parameter, Millikan determined the charge on oil droplets in mechanical equilibrium.

questions.question: Name the web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunication sharing information on mobile towers and EMF Emission Compliances.
questions.questionHtml: Name the web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunication sharing information on mobile towers and EMF Emission Compliances.
questions.solution: Tarang Sanchar is a web portal launched by the Department of Telecom (DoT), Ministry of Communications, to provide information on mobile towers and EMF Emission Compliances. questions.question: In which year did Hans Christian Oersted discover that a compass needle gets deflected when an electric current passes through a metallic wire placed nearby?
questions.questionHtml: In which year did Hans Christian Oersted discover that a compass needle gets deflected when an electric current passes through a metallic wire placed nearby?
questions.solution: In 1820, Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a compass needle deflects when an electric current passes through a nearby metallic wire, demonstrating a direct relationship between electricity and magnetism. This pivotal experiment laid the foundation for electromagnetism, influencing future scientific research and technological advancements like electric motors and generators.

questions.question: In 1830, which American scientist created the world's most powerful electromagnet, the Alnany magnet, which could lift up to 750 pounds of metal at a time?
questions.questionHtml: In 1830, which American scientist created the world's most powerful electromagnet, the Alnany magnet, which could lift up to 750 pounds of metal at a time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Joseph Henry.

Key Points

  • Joseph Henry:-
    • He was an American scientist who is best known for his work in electromagnetism. He discovered the phenomenon of self-induction and mutual induction independently of Michael Faraday.
    • In 1830, Joseph Henry created the world's most powerful electromagnet, the Albany magnet, which could lift up to 750 pounds of metal at a time. This was a significant achievement in the field of electromagnetism. 

Additional Information

  • John Cockcroft:-
    • He was a British physicist who is known for his work on the splitting of the atom.
    • He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1951 for his contributions to nuclear physics.
  • William Gilbert:-
    • He was an English physician and natural philosopher who is known as the father of electrical studies.
    • He is credited with the discovery of the Earth's magnetic field and the invention of the term "electricity."
  • Edward Purcell:-
    • He was an American physicist who is known for his work on nuclear magnetic resonance.
    • He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1952 for his contributions to the development of the nuclear magnetic resonance method.

questions.question: Which geostationary weather satellite launched by the European Space Agency in 1977 that provides weather imaging of Earth at both visible light and infrared wavelengths?
questions.questionHtml: Which geostationary weather satellite launched by the European Space Agency in 1977 that provides weather imaging of Earth at both visible light and infrared wavelengths?
questions.solution: Meteosat-1, launched by the European Space Agency (ESA) in 1977, was the first in a series of geostationary weather satellites. It significantly enhanced weather forecasting and climate research, particularly for Europe and Africa, by capturing images of Earth's surface and atmosphere in both visible light and infrared wavelengths. This capability allowed for continuous 24-hour observation of weather phenomena. ESA is one of the world's major space agencies, alongside NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), CNSA (China), ISRO (India), and others. ISRO, established in 1969, has conducted notable missions like Aryabhata, Mars Orbiter Mission, and Chandrayaan.

questions.question: Which French chemist was one of the first scientists to synthesise organic compounds such as formic acid, methane and acetylene from their elements?
questions.questionHtml: Which French chemist was one of the first scientists to synthesise organic compounds such as formic acid, methane and acetylene from their elements?
questions.solution: Marcellin Berthelot was a French chemist who was one of the pioneers in synthesising organic compounds from inorganic compounds. He developed the Thomsen-Berthelot principle of thermochemistry and conducted studies on reaction rates, hydrocarbons, alcohols, and carboxylic acids. He also researched explosive mechanisms and discovered several compounds of coal tar.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of India's first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a part of India's first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit?
questions.solution:
Saline Solution is not a part of India's first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit.

Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Sciences (INMAS) has developed India’s first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit.

The kit may ensure protection from serious injuries and faster healing of wounds resulting from nuclear warfare or radioactive leakage.

Content of the kit:-

  • Prussian blue tablets - provides 100 per cent absorption from the gut and other portals of entry to the human body and are highly effective in incorporating Radio Cesium (Cs-137) and Radio Thallium.
  • Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) injection - traps uranium in the guts and blood of victims during a nuclear accident or warfare.
  • Ca-EDTA Respiratory Fluid - inhalation formula for chelation, or grabbing, of heavy metals and radioactive elements deposited in lungs through inhalation at nuclear accident sites. When injected into the veins, it “grabs” heavy metals and minerals and removes them from the body.
  • Anti-gamma ray skin ointment - protects and heals the radiation damage on the skin.
  • Amifostine injection -  conventional radiopharmaceutical that limits damage from gamma radiation.
  • Radioactive urine/biofluid collector - can safely dispose of the urine of a person affected by radiation.

questions.question: ______ based farming system is developed to improve environmental control over production of fish.
questions.questionHtml: ______ based farming system is developed to improve environmental control over production of fish.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "Biofloc".

Important Points

  • Biofloc technology was developed in the 1990s as a way for fish and shrimp farmers to conserve feed inputs and utilize wastewater during production.
  • The main concept is that producers could piggyback off the nitrogen cycle and let beneficial bacterial colonies proliferate in culture water.
  • To achieve Biofloc, producers needed to maintain a higher carbon to nitrogen ratio in their ponds.
  • This would stimulate the growth of heterogeneous bacteria – microbes that break down organic carbon from the surrounding environment.
  • The bacterial growth (flocs) could consume nitrogenous fish wastes and toxic metabolites before being eaten by the cultured species.
  • This would reduce both the environmental footprint of production and feed costs.

Additional Information

  • Bottom-dwelling species like shrimp and tilapia are best suited to biofloc production.
  • Since the bacterial load in the water is constantly shifting, fish must be relatively resistant to environmental challenges.
  • Sensitive species will not thrive in this environment.
